summary: Kananaskis summit lookout, first built in 1929; a 2026 article says an observer still staffs it, but the summit path is closed to visitors.

facts.design: Lumber cabin on the summit, held to the peak by cables fastened to iron clasps set in eight cement blocks (1937 description)

access.note: The Kananaskis Administration closed the single path trail through the scree slope to the summit.

visit.trail_note: Summit path closed; the lookout is an active fire lookout, so do not try to reach it.

events.note: First lookout structure on the summit, per the Canada Lookouts history (drawing on a 1998 guidebook). A fire road was built to reach the lookout the same year.
A ranger from the lookout discovered a blaze in the Big Horn district, per a Winnipeg Free Press item quoted on the Canada Lookouts page.
Bow River forest reserve supervisor said his men would again staff this post and four others (Calgary Herald, as quoted).
Dexter Champion had spent three and a half seasons on the lookout (Calgary Herald, as quoted).
Second lookout on the site completed.
Third structure on the site built. The source does not say whether it is the structure standing today.
An observer spends the peak fire season in the summit lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Bragg Creek guide says a forestry officer is stationed in the lookout from May through September. The province says its lookout sites are generally staffed from April to October. The story gives the local guide's season for this summit and the provincial range as a general figure.

notes_for_editor: The 1930 and 1937 items and the 1929 blaze item are Calgary Herald and Winnipeg Free Press reports as transcribed on the Canada Lookouts page; I did not check the originals. That page's 1930 transcription contains a typo ('would again commands posts'); the quote is kept exact. The 1998 guidebook (Mike Potter) is cited only through that page. Record values not used: height 2 m and kind 'ground' are not supported (the sources describe a cabin on the summit; the 2,437 m figure in Wikipedia is the mountain's height), so height is left out and the record's kind needs a human decision. The record's 1974 build year matches the third structure, but no source says that structure is the one standing today, and the story does not claim that it is. Record coordinates (50.938941, -114.837913) match the summit coordinates in Wikipedia; the Bragg Creek page's coordinates are for the day-use area. The Bragg Creek page is undated and the closure may have changed: check with Kananaskis Country before publishing the access statement. No photo with a clear licence was found, so none is listed. No source I read names the agency that runs this summit lookout today (the record says Alberta Wildfire). The Alberta bears page refers only to wildfire staff with Agriculture and Forestry, across many sites, so the story names no agency.
